<p style="font-size:17px;">This is the California gull, <em>Larus californicus</em> (Lawrence, 1854). It is subs. <em>californicus</em>.</p>
<p style="font-size:17px;"><img alt="California gull Larus californicus Ad 1" border="0" height="399" src="images/california-gull-larus-californicus-ad_1.jpg" style="display:block;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;" title="California gull-Larus californicus-Ad_1.jpg" width="600"/></p>
<p style="font-size:17px;"><img alt="California gull Larus californicus 3cy 7" border="0" height="399" src="images/california-gull-larus-californicus-3cy_7.jpg" style="display:block;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;" title="California gull-Larus californicus-3cy_7.jpg" width="600"/></p>
<p style="font-size:17px;"><img alt="California gull Larus californicus 3cy 1" border="0" height="399" src="images/california-gull-larus-californicus-3cy_1.jpg" style="display:block;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;" title="California gull-Larus californicus-3cy_1.jpg" width="600"/></p>
<p style="font-size:17px;">Here we see the white mirrors in P9 and P10, which are characteristic, and the white trailing edge to inner wing. This (both photos of same individual) is an adult (at least 4cy) with the winter plumage (hindneck has dense brown streaks). These first three photos were taken at Wilder Ranch State Park, Santa Cruz, along the coast line.</p>
<p style="font-size:17px;"><img alt="California gull Larus californicus 062" border="0" height="397" src="images/california-gull-larus-californicus-062.jpg" style="display:block;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;" title="California gull Larus californicus 062.jpg" width="600"/></p>
<p style="font-size:17px;"><img alt="California gull Larus californicus 3cy  California gull Larus californicus 3cy" border="0" height="399" src="images/california-gull-larus-californicus-3cy-california-gull-larus-californicus-3cy.jpg" style="display:block;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;" title="California gull Larus californicus 3cy  California gull Larus californicus 3cy.jpg" width="600"/></p>
<p style="font-size:17px;">A detail of the wonderful head of this gull (same individual in these two photos, an ad). Note the dark iris, and the color pattern in the bill ring (black with red-orange tinted patch in the lower mandible). The bill is characteristically 4-colored: yellowish at the base, black ring, red-orange dot and ivory tip- this separates it from Ring-billed and Herring. The leg color is also characteristic (green-bluish) but apparently is very variable. I saw other ad birds with very yellow legs. These two photos were taken in San Lorenzo Park, Santa Cruz, CA.</p>
<p style="font-size:17px;"><img alt="California gull Larus californicus 3cy" border="0" height="399" src="images/california-gull-larus-californicus-3cy.jpg" style="display:block;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;" title="California gull-Larus californicus 3cy.jpg" width="600"/></p>
<p style="font-size:17px;">This is a 3cy bird, finishing molt to 3rd winter. The bill ring is wholly black; there are no white patches on P feathers, nor white mirrors. The bill is longer than in Ring-billed and the head is more massive. The photo was taken at Moss Landing, Elkhorn Slough, CA.</p>
<p style="font-size:17px;"><img alt="California gull Larus californicus 2cy 6" border="0" height="400" src="images/california-gull-larus-californicus-2cy_6.jpg" style="display:block;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;" title="California gull-Larus californicus-2cy_6.jpg" width="600"/></p>
<p style="font-size:17px;">This is a 1cy bird (juvenile molting into 1st winter plumage), with characteristic black-tipped bill with pale pink in the base. It has not yet started te molt of the scapulars, yet some grayish ones seem to be apparent- the median coverts look worn and faded, creating pale midwing-panel; so the bird is a bit delayed in its molt.</p>
